notes:
Top-level summary:
- Mid-market CCaaS provider focused on automated chat deflection + agent assist for ecommerce + telco customers. Heavy emphasis on unit economics.
- Current stack: Zendesk + RelayHub conversational front-end; backend ticketing + routing in-house.
- Primary ask: push deflection to 50%+ for low-friction queries while keeping cost per resolved conversation < $0.12.

Recent timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-01-20: Intro call (Avery/Ravi) — overview of Redwood capabilities; emphasized dedicated capacity for predictable burst handling.
- 2026-02-11: Deep-dive with Infra + Sec (Linnea present) — asked for SOC2 + KMS details; sent security FAQ (drive link).
- 2026-02-25: Product demo (Ravi) — walked through streaming + function/tool calling; customer liked tool-calling for order lookup. Fireflies id linked.
- 2026-03-02: Cost modeling email thread — customer asked for 3 options: hosted low-touch, reserved dedicated, and optimize-led hybrid.
- 2026-03-09: SE spike modelling review; validated that Redwood batching/caching could reduce per-token consumption by ~30% on FAQ patterns.

POC scope proposed:
- 4-week focused POC: ingest 90 days of anonymized transcripts -> evaluate deflection and cost.
- Benchmarks: 99th percentile latency target for conversational responses < 450ms (customer requirement during spikes), sustained throughput 5k concurrent sessions during peak.
- Quality gates: human-verified correctness sample 1k responses, deflection lift >= 40% to be considered successful.
- Cost controls: use caching/prefix-KV for top 200 intents, routing to quantized variants for short answers, fallback to small LLM for triage.

Technical requirements & constraints (shorthand):
- Data residency: US only for some customers -> need region pinning.
- SSO for admin console (SAML) + SCIM provisioning.
- Audit logs retention 1 year, must integrate with customer SIEM.
- KMS integration mandatory for keys at rest.
- Support for on-prem connector later for air-gapped retailer account.

Model & performance preferences (customer input):
- Prefer smaller quantized models for high-frequency, low-complexity replies (8-bit/4-bit exploration).
- Use larger model variants for escalation/liberation of complex, sensitive issues.
- Want Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization to estimate unit economics.

Cost/unit economics notes (from Cost Modeling thread):
- Customer expects target cost per conversational interaction (fully resolved) <= $0.12; current internal cost ~ $0.28 using hosted API + no caching.
- Traffic: ~10M incoming messages/mo; expected to grow 35%/yr. Peak concurrency modelled at 5k sessions.
- Interested in committed throughput (Dedicated) vs. pay-as-you-go (Hosted) tradeoffs.

Integration & operations requirements:
- Native Zendesk app + ServiceNow ticket injection.
- Tool-calling integration: order_lookup, account_merge, refund_initiate. Must support authenticated tool calls with request signing.
- Retries and graceful degradation: automatic fallback to human queue if model returns low-confidence or if latency > 1s.

Quotes & meeting snippets:
- "If we can't prove 40% deflection at the current accuracy bar and halve our unit cost, procurement won't move forward." — VP Product
- "We need hard numbers on how caching + quantization move the needle. Can you run a mock with our top 20 intents?" — Head of ML

Open items / next actions (short):
- SE bench: run throughput test w/ 8-bit quantized model + prefix cache (target 5k concurrent) by 2026-03-15.
- Send POC SOW + pricing options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Hybrid) by 2026-03-12.
- Security: provide KMS integration runbook and SOC2 evidence.
- Legal: get DP addendum draft to customer legal team (Linnea owning).

Blockers (restated): security sign-off window (expected 3 weeks), vendor economics approval from procurement, minor open question on retention window for conversational logs.

CRM style notes: shorthand, fragments, sometimes repeated asks. See Drive docs for pricing deck + security FAQ.
